# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Rowan Lawson**
[Street address]
[City], GA [ZIP]

[Date]

Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield
Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-23**
- **Member:** Rowan Lawson
- **Member ID:** W383949058
- **Reference number:** POC-F37F115FED-48372
- **Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
- **Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon), https://files.providernews.anthem.com/4827/pdf-Spine-Surgery-2024-10-20.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the lumbar decompression surgery (CPT 63030) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-23 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Anthem to reconsider that decision, because the criteria published in the plan's own *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* line up point for point with what is already in my medical records.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice, which gives a deadline of **2027-02-19**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Documentation submitted with the request.** The guideline states:

> "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of components that I do not have in front of me. My surgeon submitted a prior authorization packet containing my symptom history, conservative treatment records, imaging, and exam findings. If the plan believes a specific component from that list is missing, I ask that the reviewer identify it by name so it can be supplied.

**2. Conservative management — the combination the plan describes.** The guideline states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records document exactly that combination:

- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, 10 weeks, from 2026-04-20 to 2026-06-29, with 18 visits completed. This is recorded in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Complementary strategies:** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-13 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

The guideline also states:

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management (Physical therapy optional)"

My documented course of physical therapy ran 10 weeks, which exceeds the 6 weeks the policy names, and it was paired with medication and injection therapy.

**3. Compliance with the plan of therapy.** The guideline states:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

Eighteen completed visits across a 10-week supervised course, with a discharge note, is documentation of compliance. I completed the treatment that was prescribed to me.

**4. Completion of the course and the result.** The guideline states:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

and

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

My physical therapy course was completed and I was discharged. My records describe 24 months of **progressive** pain in the lower back, unrelieved by rest; NSAIDs gave inadequate relief; the injection helped for only 2 weeks. I did the conservative care, and it did not resolve my condition.

**5. Radicular pain with functional impairment and correlating exam findings.** The guideline states:

> "Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as:"

That sentence also ends in a colon, introducing examples I was not given. What my records state is: radicular pain into the right calf; positive provocative testing on the affected side; and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. My physical exam findings and my imaging point to the same place.

The guideline further states:

> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records state that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes. For the specific numeric pain rating and the itemized list of activities of daily living affected, I ask that the reviewer consult the office notes in the file; to make this easy, my treating records reflect [pain rating as documented in the office note of [date]] and [the specific ADLs/IADLs listed in the chart]. I am not supplying numbers here that my summary does not already contain.

**6. Imaging that correlates with the clinical findings.** The guideline states:

> "Imaging studies. All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

and

> "Documentation of nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on MRI or other advanced imaging performed within the past 6 months that correlates with clinical findings"

My MRI of the lumbar spine was performed on **2026-06-30** — within six months of the request that was denied — and it shows **L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root**. That is nerve root compression, documented on advanced imaging, on the same side as my symptoms: my radicular pain goes into my right calf, my provocative testing is positive on the affected side, and my neurologic deficit corresponds to the imaged level. The imaging and the clinical picture agree. The MRI report was produced by [radiologist name / imaging facility, per the report in the file], and I ask that the report itself be reviewed.

**7. Other sources of pain.** The guideline states:

> "All other reasonable sources of pain have been ruled out"

My records note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoker. My surgeon's workup addressing this criterion is in the prior authorization packet, and I ask that it be reviewed against this requirement.

**8. Provisions that waive the conservative care requirement.** I want to note, without overstating my own records, that the guideline contains these provisions:

> "The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when cauda equina syndrome or conus medullaris syndrome is present, and urgent intervention is indicated."

> "Progressive or severe neurologic deficits secondary to cauda equina, lateral recess or foraminal compression (conservative management requirement waived)"

> "Acute neurologic deterioration including signs and symptoms of cauda equina syndrome, or rapid progression of neurologic deficits confirmed by imaging, regardless of underlying pathology."

My records document severe right lateral recess stenosis with compression of the traversing L5 nerve root, a neurologic deficit corresponding to that level, and 24 months of progressive symptoms. I ask the reviewer to consider whether these provisions apply to my case. In any event, I did complete conservative care, so I do not need to rely on a waiver.

**9. The herniation criteria sets.** The guideline states:

> "Initial disc herniation when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

and

> "Recurrent disc herniation when BOTH criteria are met: • Requirements for initial herniation • Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management"

The first of these ends in a colon and introduces a list of criteria that I was not given in full. I ask the plan to identify which criteria set it applied to my request and which specific element it found unmet, so that I can respond to it directly.

## A note on what I am and am not quoting

The only language I have placed in quotation marks above is text from the plan's own *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery*. Where that guideline lists further conditions I was not provided, I have said so rather than guessing at them. I have not restated any threshold — any number of weeks, visits, or severity grade — that does not appear in the language quoted above.

## What I am asking Anthem to do

I respectfully ask that Anthem:

1. Overturn the denial of CPT 63030 and authorize the surgery my surgeon has documented that I need; or
2. If the denial is maintained, tell me in writing the specific criterion from the *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* that my records do not meet, the specific documentation that would satisfy it, and the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination.

I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with experience in spine surgery, and that my full prior authorization packet — the physical therapy discharge note, the injection record, the MRI report of 2026-06-30, and Dr. Reyes's operative recommendation — be part of the review file. Please let me know if any additional records would help; I will provide them promptly.

I have been dealing with this pain for two years. I completed the physical therapy, I took the medication, I had the injection, and I am still unable to stand for more than ten minutes. My surgeon has documented why this procedure is needed, and my records track the plan's own published criteria. I would be grateful for a careful second look.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Lawson**
Member ID: W383949058
Reference number: POC-F37F115FED-48372
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date signed]

**Enclosures:** [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-23] · [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-20 to 2026-06-29] · [MRI lumbar spine report, 2026-06-30] · [Office notes from Dr. Reyes] · [Medication and injection records]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
